report:
Reviewed the complete claim, the sole implementation association in sage_meta::todo in service_spec.rs, and the complete sole annotated test todo::meta_validation_claim_specific_evidence. Additional captured dependencies are the review specification and repository review/documentation workflow instructions. This is acceptance of explicitly deferred evidence, not certification that the repository already meets the universal documentation-evidence guarantee.

The requirements are: evidence belongs to an individual architectural claim; positive established-behavior statements identify evidence exercising that behavior; negative or partial artifacts may document limitations; aggregate suite success cannot establish an unstated local guarantee; and documentation review must match every implemented capability to a focused test, snapshot, normalized trace, edit experiment, exact oracle result, inspector scenario, or source anchor whose assertions match the capability. The implementation TODO explicitly identifies the missing universal coverage: automatic claim-test reviews exist but supporting prose does not yet have complete claim-specific evidence for every positive capability. Thus it honestly leaves claim-specific mapping and the exhaustive capability audit deferred, including semantic matching rather than simply checking that an association exists. It does not claim that aggregate success fills this gap. The allowance for negative/partial artifacts is consistent with retaining this explicit limitation as TODO evidence.

The annotated test is an empty TODO function, with a comment specifying the full documentation review scenario and acceptable evidence forms. It has no assertions and proves none of the positive requirements, including rejection of mismatched or aggregate-only evidence. Its prerequisite is completion and review of the supporting-prose capability inventory and the claim-specific associations/artifacts named by the implementation and test TODOs. Completing that work must identify each positive claim's actual asserted behavior, retain limited or negative outcomes as such, and associate substantive focused checks before replacing the placeholder. A plausible missing/mismatched local assertion would not be detected by this placeholder; that is the acknowledged deferred coverage, not implemented protection. There are no ordinary or N/A entries to assess and no essential production helper is relied upon to claim this universal behavior is implemented.

Executed cargo meta review start and recorded review read commands; no behavioral tests were run. Running the empty placeholder would add no semantic evidence. The existing implementation and test TODOs adequately disclose the missing audit and evidence, so no edits are requested and deferred status must remain visible.
